presentation.summary: Manage scaffold access, fall protection, dropped objects and worsening weather during work 12 metres above an offshore deck.
presentation.role: You are the work-at-height safety lead for maintenance on an offshore module.
presentation.situation: Technicians must work from an altered scaffold high above deck. The task creates fall, dropped-object and weather-related hazards over an access route used by other personnel.
presentation.objective: Keep access, fall prevention, dropped-object controls and weather limits effective throughout the job.
peopleInvolved: Personnel using the lower access route
knownFacts: The scaffold was altered before the job.
Work requires reaching near the platform edge.
Tools and fittings are used above occupied areas.
Wind conditions can change quickly offshore.

work_at_height_permit.title: Work-at-height permit
work_at_height_permit.summary: Work-at-height permit defines the authorized scope, conditions, hold points and required controls for the work.
work_at_height_permit.details:
Check that the scope and location match the actual task.
Confirm required controls and hold points are satisfied.
Treat changed conditions as a trigger for reassessment.

access_decision_defensible.observable: The action improves control at the verify safe access stage, but one important verification or scope gap remains. Work proceeds with less assurance.
access_decision_defensible.guidedInsight: This is professionally plausible and partly correct, but it leaves one material criterion unresolved compared with the BEST action.

access_decision_best.observable: The team verifies the decisive safeguards at the verify safe access stage before exposure continues. The work-at-height task moves forward from a controlled condition.
access_decision_best.guidedInsight: The BEST option closes the important uncertainty before work proceeds. It controls the hazard through verification rather than assumption.

access_decision_weak.observable: Preparation or work continues while a significant control question remains unresolved at the verify safe access stage. The available recovery margin decreases.
access_decision_weak.guidedInsight: The action contains a valid element, but sequencing is weak because work advances before the decisive safeguard has been verified.

access_decision_critical.observable: The work-at-height task proceeds on an unsupported assumption at the verify safe access stage. A critical safeguard is bypassed and risk escalates sharply.
access_decision_critical.guidedInsight: A critical choice often sounds efficient because it relies on prior status, appearance or experience. High-hazard work requires positive verification of the critical barrier.

dropped_object_decision_best.guidedInsight: The BEST option closes the important uncertainty before work proceeds. It controls the hazard through verification rather than assumption.

weather_decision_defensible.observable: The team pauses part of the activity and gathers more information, but some exposure or uncertainty remains during the respond to worsening wind stage.
weather_decision_defensible.guidedInsight: This choice recognizes the change, yet it leaves a narrower safety margin than a full stop-and-reassess response.

weather_decision_weak.observable: The work continues under modified monitoring or local precautions even though the respond to worsening wind condition has changed materially. Risk begins to rise.
weather_decision_weak.guidedInsight: Extra observation is not equivalent to restoring a failed or uncertain barrier. Changed conditions should be controlled, not merely watched.

weather_decision_best.observable: The team stops or stabilizes the work when conditions change at the respond to worsening wind stage. The new condition is verified before the task continues.
weather_decision_best.guidedInsight: Changing conditions invalidate earlier assumptions. The BEST response creates a deliberate hold point and reassesses the controls before exposure continues.

weather_decision_critical.observable: The changed condition is effectively accepted and the work-at-height task continues. A critical barrier is lost and the scenario moves into emergency territory.
weather_decision_critical.guidedInsight: Proceeding because an alarm limit, schedule or visible condition has not yet become extreme can miss the earlier point where safe intervention was still easy.

closeout_decision_defensible.observable: The team strengthens the immediate controls and uses a controlled restart review, but the closeout does not explore the underlying failure as completely as the BEST path.
closeout_decision_defensible.guidedInsight: Corrective action is valuable, but restart assurance is stronger when the underlying cause and all affected safeguards are verified.

closeout_decision_best.observable: The work-at-height task remains suspended while causes, damaged safeguards and corrective actions are verified. Work is reauthorized only after a safe basis is re-established.
closeout_decision_best.guidedInsight: Safe closeout is not simply returning conditions to normal. It must address why control was lost and verify the barriers needed for a safe restart.

closeout_decision_weak.observable: The team corrects the most visible problem and prepares to resume the work-at-height task before the full causal chain has been resolved.
closeout_decision_weak.guidedInsight: A technically acceptable local fix can still be weak if it restores production before learning and system-level corrections are complete.

closeout_decision_critical.observable: The work-at-height task is pushed toward restart after only superficial recovery. Critical causes or damaged safeguards remain unresolved.
closeout_decision_critical.guidedInsight: Restart pressure can recreate the same hazard. A major event is more likely when work resumes before critical barriers are restored and verified.

safe_completion.title: Safe completion
safe_completion.narrative: The work-at-height task was completed with the critical hazards controlled and changing conditions managed before escalation.
safe_completion.keyTurningPoint: You kept the work within verified scaffold, fall-protection and weather controls.

controlled_recovery.title: Controlled recovery
controlled_recovery.narrative: The work-at-height task developed a significant control weakness, but later decisions restored a controlled state before serious harm occurred.
controlled_recovery.keyTurningPoint: A work-at-height control weakened, but the task was stopped and recovered before harm occurred.

incident_contained.title: Incident contained
incident_contained.narrative: The scenario developed into an incident, but emergency and recovery actions contained the event and limited its consequences.
incident_contained.keyTurningPoint: An object or weather event occurred, but exclusion and stop-work actions limited consequences.

major_incident.title: Major incident
major_incident.narrative: Unresolved control failures allowed the work-at-height task to escalate into a major incident requiring extended response, investigation and corrective action.
major_incident.keyTurningPoint: Several height-related barriers degraded and exposed people above and below the worksite.

critical_failure.title: Critical failure
critical_failure.narrative: The decision path produced a severe uncontrolled outcome in the work-at-height task. Recovery options were overwhelmed by a critical barrier failure.
critical_failure.keyTurningPoint: A critical fall or dropped-object safeguard was bypassed while exposure remained.
